question: Which patients can safely stop treatment, and can that group be enlarged?
why_it_matters: Withdrawal trials are run in bDMARD-treated populations, in which sustained drug-free remission essentially never occurs (0%), while 37% of never-bDMARD patients achieved it at 5 years. Current guidance may generalise from the wrong population.
what_would_resolve_it: Withdrawal RCT enriched for never-bDMARD, autoantibody-negative patients in sustained remission with no power-Doppler synovitis.

question: Why is ACPA-negative at-risk disease apparently preventable while ACPA-positive is not?
why_it_matters: TREAT EARLIER 5-year showed RA in 9% vs 32% (HR 0.24, NNT 4) in ACPA-negative at-risk participants and no effect in ACPA-positive. If real, this is the first genuine prevention signal in RA.
what_would_resolve_it: Independent replication in an ACPA-negative-enriched at-risk RCT, pre-specified rather than post-hoc.

question: Can molecular stratification become a validated treatment-allocation tool?
why_it_matters: Synovial transcriptomic models reach AUC 0.75-0.87 for response and multidrug resistance, but no biomarker is in routine use; drug selection remains sequential trial-and-error costing 3-6 months per failed cycle.
what_would_resolve_it: Prospective biomarker-stratified randomised allocation trial with the biomarker fixed in advance.
current_evidence_tier: Probable for prediction; no evidence for clinical utility

question: What maintains inflammation in persistent inflammatory refractory RA (PIRRA), and is it stromal?
why_it_matters: A stromal/fibroblast signature marks multidrug resistance; spatial data describe fibrogenic vascular niches expanding after immune depletion. If disease is stromally autonomous, a new drug class is needed rather than another immune target.
what_would_resolve_it: Interventional test of a fibroblast- or TGF-beta/Notch-directed agent in ultrasound-confirmed PIRRA; longitudinal paired synovial biopsy through treatment failure.

question: What should be done for non-inflammatory refractory RA (NIRRA)?
why_it_matters: 43% of difficult-to-treat patients have high disease activity scores without objective inflammation, with higher BMI and 15% fibromyalgia prevalence. They currently receive escalating immunosuppression with no mechanistic rationale and no established alternative.
what_would_resolve_it: Define NIRRA prospectively by imaging, then randomise non-immunosuppressive strategies against treatment escalation using pain/fatigue/function endpoints.
current_evidence_tier: Established as a phenomenon; no established treatment

question: Is autoantibody-negative RA one disease?
why_it_matters: Different genetics, different environmental associations, 26.6% 10-year drug-free remission, 12.8% 10-year diagnosis change, and apparent preventability. Pooling with seropositive disease may average away real effects.
what_would_resolve_it: Serostatus-stratified re-analysis of existing trial datasets plus a dedicated seronegative inception cohort with deep phenotyping.

question: What is the true attributable fraction of modifiable exposures?
why_it_matters: Population twin data give additive genetic variance 12% (0-76%) and shared environment 50% (0-72%), which is compatible with a far larger modifiable component than the commonly quoted ~60% heritability implies.
what_would_resolve_it: Large modern twin/family designs with autoantibody stratification; exposure-specific attributable-fraction estimation in linked registry cohorts.

question: Is the window of opportunity biological or artefactual?
why_it_matters: Earlier treatment associates with better outcomes, but the strongest study is a 20-per-arm case-control, no RCT has randomised time-to-treatment, and the duration-response gradient is absent in smokers.
what_would_resolve_it: A randomised delayed-start design in newly presenting RA, or instrumental-variable analysis exploiting referral-time variation.
current_evidence_tier: Probable for the association; uncertain for the mechanism

question: Can immune tolerance be induced rather than immunity suppressed?
why_it_matters: Peresolimab is the first clinical test of agonising an inhibitory checkpoint (PD-1) in RA; CAR T-cell therapy is entering autoimmune disease. Both would in principle allow drug-free disease control.
what_would_resolve_it: Dose-ranging and durability trials with drug-free follow-up as a pre-specified endpoint, not just disease activity change.

question: Why the joint, and why symmetrically?
why_it_matters: No current causal model explains the anatomical specificity or symmetry of RA. An answer would reframe the mucosal-origins continuum and possibly identify the localisation step as a target.
what_would_resolve_it: Comparative tissue profiling of affected vs spared joints in the same patient during the transition from at-risk to clinical arthritis.
